"Eh, the AI's responses aren't determined by user input."

Sorry, that's absolutely untrue.  Perhaps you meant the length of the AI's responses.  To a first order, those are determined by whatever system prompt [c.ai](http://c.ai) feeds to the model. Users and creators have no control over that beyond choosing the model.

As for the content of the response, the character definition will prevail in the earliest responses, but a determined user can completely alter the the bot's behavior once the conversation gets beyond a trivial length.

OP is on target when they say, "t feels like the generation is eating off of itself which makes it easy for the responses to repeat the same phrases all the time."

No argument about the number of badly defined bots, though.

Yeah, no problem. Here is what you do on the app. 

1. Go to your profile page. 

2. Tap the gear cog for settings.

3. In settings there is an area called “accessibility”. Tap it. 

4. Once in accessbility, choose your chat color. Picking color will keep it blue. Picking monochrome will make the chat bubbles grey.

5. Adjust the contrast and saturation to your liking. There is a sliding bar for both and it has an example display for what your chat will look like, so you can make sure the color will be acceptable for you.

(And just to be clear I don't mean all fans of a person, I mean ones who are overly attached or even obsessed.) There's also thinking about it from the celebrity's perspective and how they might consider it offensive and creepy since something is speaking for them that isn't actually them.
